experiments.design: Prepared protein + ligand → pretrained Nesso [frozen] → two affinity vectors → continuous readouts [PXR-fitted] → 6 − mean output. The original specification proposed staged calibration, head tuning and deeper adaptation.
experiments.limits: Nesso predicts distograms and scalar affinity; it is not a cofolder that generates coordinates. Numerical affinity conversion does not make binding and cellular activation biologically equivalent.
experiments.question: Does adapting Nesso improve PXR activity prediction, compete with ligand-only models, and add complementary information?
experiments.result: The initial matched nested comparison answered yes to improvement over native, no to beating rich 2D descriptors. Later experiments refine the complementarity answer rather than erase this starting point.
experiments.summary_message: Head adaptation improves on the native continuous score, but ligand-only LightGBM remains stronger.
experiments.title: Conception: can binding features predict cellular activation?

experiments.design: Two cached 384D vectors [frozen] → twin pretrained continuous MLPs [fitted]. Five nested chemical-family folds; inner selection and three-seed refits. The matched rich 2D LightGBM selects features within training folds.
experiments.limits: Historical 714-row qualified lockbox, later all-790 validation, and 513 challenge rows are distinct cohorts. These retrospective raw-MAE scores are not the later low-data weighted scores.
experiments.question: How much can the final regression heads recover?
experiments.result: Development raw MAE: native 0.915, tuned heads 0.633, rich 2D 0.516. Both learned models compress the highest-potency tail.
experiments.summary_message: Both fitted models compress the potent tail despite lower overall error for LightGBM.
experiments.title: Initial head-only versus rich 2D

experiments.design: Frozen vectors → training-selected ridge or shallow MLP; compare expanded nested learning rates, target/loss sensitivities, residual ridge and learned stacking. Encoders remain frozen.
experiments.limits: These controls cannot identify a protein-specific causal effect. Opened validation is retrospective.
experiments.question: Is useful information in the vectors, or only in the pretrained nonlinear heads?
experiments.result: Frozen mean-vector ridge reaches about 0.633 raw development MAE with better ranking than the original heads. Expanding optimization does not close the descriptor gap; much useful signal is linearly accessible.
experiments.summary_message: Frozen-vector ridge recovers substantial PXR signal without the pretrained nonlinear heads.
experiments.title: Transfer, learning-rate sensitivity and frozen probes

experiments.design: Frozen affinity representations → matched random-initialized readouts of different capacities [fitted using nested training selection].
experiments.limits: Only downstream capacity changes; upstream pretraining is not ablated.
experiments.question: Does greater nonlinear readout capacity help?
experiments.result: The completed CPU capacity matrix separates architecture from released-head initialization; larger readouts do not establish a solution to the persistent descriptor gap. Consult the complete per-model table rather than select a single favorable run.
experiments.summary_message: Extra readout capacity changes error modestly and inconsistently across frozen representations.
experiments.title: Readout capacity control

experiments.design: Saved compound identities → Random or Butina outer folds → matched FIT/CAL acquisitions; strict follow-up removes TEST neighbors.
experiments.limits: Butina centroid groups alone do not enforce a pairwise similarity boundary; repeated draws reuse TEST compounds.
experiments.question: How were Random, Butina and strict chemical splits used to test the models?
experiments.result: Compound-labeled saved assignments and acquisitions for each split generation.
experiments.title: Chemical splits: Random and Butina

experiments.design: Released twin heads [fitted] on frozen vectors; objective and learning rate chosen inside each outer training set; fixed weight decay isolates this comparison.
experiments.limits: Retrospective optimization evidence; freeze a recipe before testing new data.
experiments.question: Would objective selection relieve head compression?
experiments.result: The joint nested selector reaches raw development MAE 0.6224, versus 0.6330 historically. None of its development predictions exceed pEC50 6: lower average error does not solve the active tail.
experiments.summary_message: Joint loss and learning-rate selection reduces average error without restoring predictions above pEC50 6.
experiments.title: Nested loss × learning rate

experiments.design: Frozen vectors → released continuous and binary branches → training-fitted linear/quadratic mapping, or both branches [fine-tuned] with bounded fusion.
experiments.limits: Binder probability is not a cellular activity classifier. Potency thresholds are functional proxies, not binding labels; the small dual-head gain is not robust across cohorts.
experiments.question: Was evaluating only the continuous output an incomplete test of Nesso?
experiments.result: Combined quadratic calibration reaches raw development MAE 0.774; dual-branch adaptation 0.629 versus continuous-only 0.633. Dual-head challenge MAE worsens to 0.647 versus 0.601.
experiments.summary_message: Using both branches helps scalar calibration, but dual-head adaptation does not improve consistently across cohorts.
experiments.title: Binary readout correction and dual heads

experiments.design: Upstream protein-conditioned features [frozen] → all-pairs, ligand–ligand-only or receptor–ligand-only final pool → nested fitted mean-384D ridge.
experiments.limits: Ligand–ligand cells were already protein-conditioned. This does not show that Nesso ignores protein or establish a causal protein ablation.
experiments.question: Are direct receptor–ligand cells needed at the final pooling operation?
experiments.result: All 4,134 compounds extracted with zero failures and positive-control parity. Ligand-only final pooling improves raw development MAE from 0.63279 to 0.60624; all-790 validation changes 0.59630 to 0.59421 with an unresolved paired interval.
experiments.summary_message: Ligand–ligand final pooling improves development MAE, but its validation advantage is unresolved.
experiments.title: Final pair pooling — completed

experiments.design: Frozen Nesso representations or Morgan features → 12 fitted/native methods → within-budget interval calibration. Two split policies, five folds, ten paired draws, five small budgets plus full-pool reference; three neural seeds per task.
experiments.limits: N25 means 20 FIT and five CAL labels; nominal 90% intervals can be unbounded. Full-pool is an outer-training-pool reference, not all 3,344 labels.
experiments.question: How should 25–500 acquired PXR labels be spent?
experiments.result: All 7,200 task systems completed. Continuous heads are practical Nesso candidates; released initialization has no consistent advantage. Original generic MLP/ridge failures expose scaling and extrapolation problems rather than absence of feature signal.
experiments.summary_message: Continuous heads improve with more labels; the original vector probes show large, irregular errors.
experiments.title: Original low-data matrix — completed

experiments.design: Frozen native vectors → training-only stable preprocessing and fitted readout; ligand features → training-only reduction and fitted LightGBM. Strict branch purges FIT/CAL pools at Morgan similarity ≥0.35 to test. All labels remain inside the acquired budget.
experiments.limits: All 8,100 new follow-up tasks completed, plus 1,200 original comparator tasks replayed. Repeated draws are dependent; chemical novelty and prospective coverage remain unresolved.
experiments.question: Were poor vector probes an avoidable preprocessing problem?
experiments.result: Stable scaling and target centering substantially improve MLP performance; added weight decay contributes little. Stable ridge is competitive, but its small N500 advantage over the pretrained head is unresolved.
experiments.summary_message: Stable scaling and target centering reduce MLP error; adding weight decay barely changes the curve.
experiments.title: Stable scaling and readouts

experiments.design: Frozen native vectors → training-only stable preprocessing and fitted readout; ligand features → training-only reduction and fitted LightGBM. Strict branch purges FIT/CAL pools at Morgan similarity ≥0.35 to test. All labels remain inside the acquired budget.
experiments.limits: All 8,100 new follow-up tasks completed, plus 1,200 original comparator tasks replayed. Repeated draws are dependent; chemical novelty and prospective coverage remain unresolved.
experiments.question: Does a broader ligand-only baseline change the low-data conclusion?
experiments.result: Descriptor LightGBM has lower mean-task weighted error from N250 upward. N500: 0.497 versus adapted head 0.542. The head remains better within the pEC50 ≥4 stratum in this repeated-draw experiment.
experiments.summary_message: Descriptors overtake the head from N250 overall, while the head retains lower N500 error at pEC50 ≥4.
experiments.title: Stronger low-data descriptor baseline

experiments.design: Frozen native vectors → training-only stable preprocessing and fitted readout; ligand features → training-only reduction and fitted LightGBM. Strict branch purges FIT/CAL pools at Morgan similarity ≥0.35 to test. All labels remain inside the acquired budget.
experiments.limits: All 8,100 new follow-up tasks completed, plus 1,200 original comparator tasks replayed. Repeated draws are dependent; chemical novelty and prospective coverage remain unresolved.
experiments.question: Does purging neighbors change practical generalization?
experiments.result: The completed strict audit changes aggregate scores little; actual nearest-FIT similarity below 0.2 remains harder. N500 90% intervals are near 89% coverage but broad.
experiments.summary_message: Neighbor purging barely moves overall error, but the most novel strict-test predictions remain harder.
experiments.title: Strict chemical separation

experiments.archive_reason: Engineering feasibility; retained as source history, not a result experiment.
experiments.design: Real prepared input → frozen trunk → first affinity member with injected adapters [engineering updates] → parity and saved-state replay.
experiments.limits: The first pilot used an engineering objective without assay labels and only one member.
experiments.question: Can gradients reach a real upstream affinity module without changing the trunk?
experiments.result: Real-input gradient, frozen-weight, zero-update and adapter replay checks passed. This established a runnable intervention, not predictive superiority.
experiments.title: First-member upstream feasibility

experiments.archive_reason: Engineering feasibility; retained as source history, not a result experiment.
experiments.design: Eight predetermined FIT records → frozen trunk capture → each member’s tensors/RNG → continuous heads [fitted] with/without rank-4 adapters at esm_proj.1, esm_proj.3 and first transition fc1.
experiments.limits: Two SGD updates on eight records are engineering feasibility, not held-out utility. Binary weights stay frozen, but upstream changes can change binary outputs.
experiments.question: Can both actual affinity members be captured and adapted reproducibly?
experiments.result: Eight of eight records and both supervised arms completed. Native/differentiable, zero-update and saved-state replay discrepancies were exactly zero. Trainable parameters: 592,130 head-only; 616,706 with adapters.
experiments.title: Both-member capture and supervised training

experiments.design: Both affinity members: pretrained continuous heads [fitted], plus rank-4 LoRA at esm_proj.1/.3 and pairformer_stack.layers.0.transition_z.fc1 [fitted only in LoRA arm]. Main trunk and external ESM encoder frozen. N100=80 FIT+20 CAL; N500=400+100; 40 full-FIT optimizer updates, one draw and seed, no tuning.
experiments.limits: Low-potency correction supplies most net LoRA-versus-head gain; pEC50 ≥4 weighted error slightly worsens. This fixed training recipe does not exhaust optimization; no fresh holdout.
experiments.question: Does actual upstream adaptation add to the same trained heads?
experiments.result: All 20 neural fits and 30 control cells completed. N500 pooled weighted MAE: head 0.5773, LoRA 0.5610, frozen ridge 0.5345, descriptors 0.5006. N100 favors LoRA on weighted MAE but not all metrics.
experiments.summary_message: LoRA adds a small gain; descriptors lead at 500 labels
experiments.title: Matched upstream-LoRA predictive comparison

experiments.design: Saved native and adapted predictions + actual FIT-neighbor identities + MW/charge + frozen 768D native vectors → descriptive ranks, strata and PCA; nothing fitted for prospective prediction.
experiments.limits: Full-cohort PCA is descriptive. Adapted internal tensors were not analyzed; neither feature norm nor proximity proves mechanism. Low MW and low potency are different variables.
experiments.question: What distinguishes compounds whose predictions change?
experiments.result: Large movers are not merely closest FIT neighbors. Smaller compounds move more; native feature norm is associated with movement more strongly than accuracy improvement. Native PCA’s first component captures 66.8% of variance.
experiments.summary_message: Smaller compounds tend to move more under adaptation
experiments.title: Movement, chemistry and native feature geometry

experiments.design: Frozen native scalar + continuous MW → FIT-only weighted linear scaling: score only, MW only, additive score+MW, or score+MW+interaction. CAL is reserved for intervals; no threshold-based rule.
experiments.limits: The interaction is four coefficients, not MW alone. A conspicuous subgroup correction is not proof that MW explains all aggregate gains, binding, or activation biology.
experiments.question: Is the low-MW correction uniquely neural?
experiments.result: All 40 fits completed. For 237 compounds below 215 Da at N500, weighted MAE: native 1.834; LoRA 1.179; additive score+MW 1.163; interaction 0.863.
experiments.summary_message: A scalar interaction beats LoRA on small compounds—not larger ones
experiments.title: Can simple molecular-weight controls explain the correction?

experiments.design: N500 strict fold0: 400 FIT → nested grouped OOF descriptor and stable-ridge predictions → convex mixture weight [FIT-selected]; native vectors frozen. CAL outcomes unused.
experiments.limits: This is frozen-representation ridge, not LoRA. One inspected fold motivated the locked continuation; it is not independent confirmation.
experiments.question: Can a weaker standalone representation add useful complementary signal?
experiments.result: The pilot improves weighted MAE from descriptor 0.502895 to blend 0.485238, with selected Nesso weight about 0.3983. Higher-potency accuracy improves while lower-potency error worsens.
experiments.summary_message: The pilot blend helps higher potency, but hurts lower potency
experiments.title: Descriptor + frozen-Nesso hybrid pilot

experiments.design: Frozen vectors → stable ridge and ligand descriptors → LightGBM [independently FIT-selected]. Three grouped meta folds and deeper selection create honest inner OOF inputs; convex weighted-MAE mixture fitted inside FIT. Fold0 reused byte-identically; folds1–4 newly fit.
experiments.limits: The lower-potency group worsens in every fold. Weights are 1/max(SE,0.1); below4 is 31% of compounds but 16.4% of weight. Locked recipe means procedure, not one fixed mixture coefficient. No prospective holdout or retraining variability estimate.
experiments.question: Does the same training-selected blending procedure hold across the remaining folds?
experiments.result: Pooled weighted MAE improves 0.500588 → 0.486790; raw MAE 0.599636 → 0.594731; Spearman 0.656863 → 0.686392. Weighted error improves in all five folds. At pEC50 ≥4: 0.434197 → 0.411839; below4: 0.840152 → 0.870134.
experiments.summary_message: Every fold gains overall—and pays a lower-potency penalty
experiments.title: Locked hybrid — all five folds completed

experiments.design: Existing native protein/ligand/heme inference [frozen] + identity-SMILES MW → training-fold scaling and fitted OLS scalar controls → same-row pIC50 evaluation across CYP1A2, 2C9, 2D6 and 3A4.
experiments.limits: CYP uses unweighted fitting and MAE: supplied std/CI are not justified sampling SE. Do not transfer PXR’s uncertainty floor or potency threshold. This is not a general replication of the PXR effect.
experiments.question: Does the PXR MW effect recur for direct CYP inhibition?
experiments.result: Additive MW helps CYP2C9 and CYP3A4; the score–MW interaction does not consistently outperform additive. Same-CYP inhibitor baselines remain stronger overall. Small-MW groups contain only 22 / 11 / 21 / 30 compounds.
experiments.summary_message: MW helps two CYP assays; the interaction is not a general gain
experiments.title: Four-CYP transfer of scalar MW controls

experiments.design: Exact 3,344 development IDs → provider Emax/SE fields + saved native/adapted predictions → MW strata and descriptive adjustments. No model inference or predictive fitting.
experiments.limits: The proposed low normalized efficacy explanation is weakened, not established. Higher fit uncertainty is associated with size/potency, but neither scalar affinity nor low pEC50 proves binding without activation. Raw curves, control denominator and parameter covariance are unavailable; the adapter is not shown to learn efficacy.
experiments.question: Are small molecules overcalled because they bind without activating PXR?
experiments.result: Below215 versus larger: normalized Emax medians 1.240 vs 0.977; raw log2 fold-change Emax 2.17 vs 2.53; pEC50 SE 0.558 vs 0.141. All 237 small compounds pass normalized Emax ≥0.6 qualification.
experiments.summary_message: Small compounds have higher uncertainty, not lower normalized efficacy
experiments.title: Emax and uncertainty: testing the biological explanation
